authoredNote: Authored 2026-10-05 on analyzer/CORPUS_PERL3 from the source .pm above, with every line number transcribed from that file by reading it, and only then confirmed against one analyzer run. The two labels pinned here (`uses`, `references`) were both EMITTED-0 at handover and are both GAP verdicts; the counts that decided them are in script/m14/perl-construct-probe.mts over the derived 5,127-file population, and the reasoning for refusing each shape is in docs/analyzers/perl.md. Every REFUSED shape below is pinned as a forbid, because a refusal nothing tests is an oversight rather than a rule -- that is the same lesson the `overrides`-missing-from-Bash wave taught, and the same lesson this lane's own `use constant { ... }` dead branch taught twice. Lines 56 and 62 were added AFTER the first mutant run, because two of the guards they cover turned out to be untested: five mutants survived, three of them because a second guard on the same rule caught the input the forbid was written for. A forbid nothing exercises is an oversight, so the SOURCE grew the shapes its forbids were already asserting, rather than the forbids being deleted to make the suite green.
rationale:
Perl has two constructs that name a symbol WITHOUT invoking it, and the lane emitted 0 edges for either. Naming a symbol without invoking it is not `calls`: `my $cb = \&helper;` runs nothing, and a graph that files it as a call says `helper` was executed.

THE SPLIT BETWEEN THE TWO LABELS, since `src/lsp/evidence_tier.ts` rule 3 puts `reference(s)` and `use(s)` in the SAME tier and therefore cannot choose between them:

  uses        a symbol named in a VALUE position -- the thing the code uses.
              bash files a `$VAR` read this way, ruby an `@ivar` read, python an
              `obj.attr` read, php a `$this->x` read.
  references  a name a QUERY tests against, invoking nothing: a class, a role, a
              method. java files an import, python files `isinstance(x, T)`, php a
              declared type. Perl's `->isa('C')` is python's isinstance under a
              different name.

Emitting both for one construct would ship the same edge under two labels, and bb_graph would count it twice.

WHAT IS PINNED, AND WHY EACH LINE IS HERE:

  17   \&helper             uses run -> helper. A code reference: the name is
                            written and nothing is invoked.
  20   \&Code::Ref::helper  the QUALIFIED spelling of line 17. It is ONE edge, not
                            two: `addRelationship` keys on type+source+target, and
                            two calls to one leaf are one edge everywhere else in this
                            lane too. The package is not thrown away -- it is in
                            `meta.qualifiedAs`, so a reader can ask for the qualified
                            form without the graph carrying two nodes.
  24   \&helper()           the CALL is filed, the reference is not. The grammar
                            types this child as `function_call_expression`, so the
                            `uses` rule finds no `function` node under the refgen and
                            cannot fire. This line is also the pin for the `&` defect
                            it used to carry: the target was `&helper`, which is not a
                            name the indexer stores, and the same defect was 93 edges
                            in 36 corpus files before the strip landed.
  26   \&{ $self->{slot} }  REFUSED -- 3,618 corpus sites whose target is not
                            written. Nothing in the file names a sub here.
  29   \&$plain             REFUSED -- the varname is `$plain`, and the written-name
                            allowlist rejects a sigil.
  31   \@LIST               REFUSED -- a ref to an ARRAY, not to code: the refgen has
                            no `function` child at all.
  33   \$TIMEOUT            REFUSED -- a scalar ref, same reason.
  36   ->isa('Other::Class')  references run -> Class. `isa` IS invoked and `calls
                            run -> isa` is CORRECT beside it; the class is not
                            invoked, and that is the edge this label exists for.
  38   ->isa($self->{cls})  REFUSED -- 175 corpus sites where the query's name is a
                            variable. The file states no name, so an edge would name
                            a symbol the source never mentions.
  40   ->DOES('Some::Role')  references run -> Role. A role is named, not invoked.
  42   ->can('later')       references run -> later. A METHOD named, not invoked.
  44   ->can('run')         REFUSED -- self-reference by method. True of the source
                            and useless in a graph, the same rule as the self-base
                            guard on `extends`.
  46   ->isa('Code::Ref')   REFUSED -- self-reference by package: the query asks
                            about the package doing the asking.
  48   ->isa("Other::$suffix")  REFUSED -- an INTERPOLATED literal is not a name. Same
                            rule `namesAClass` already applies to a receiver.
  53   $TIMEOUT             FORBIDDEN as a `uses` edge. This is the measured gap and
                            it is pinned as ABSENT so it cannot be mistaken for an
                            oversight: reading a package global the file itself
                            declares is 2 sites in 40 files on the probe's first pass,
                            against 850 DECLARATION sites. Perl's package globals are
                            written far more often than they are read, so a `uses`
                            branch on them would be a large branch over almost nothing.
                            Declared in the lane doc's limitations with its number.

NO BRANCH EXISTS for two shapes with a measured ZERO, and their absence is the point:
`UNIVERSAL::isa($x, 'C')` is 0 sites in 5,127 files and `bless $x, 'Class'` is 0 in
5,127 (the idiom is `bless $self, $class`, 736 sites, where the class is a VARIABLE).
A branch for a construct the corpus does not contain is dead code by this lane's own
standard, so the zero is a recorded ruling instead of an unreachable `if`.

TWO LINES ADDED BECAUSE FIVE MUTANTS SURVIVED, and what that survival measured.
Three of the surviving mutants removed a guard that a SECOND guard on the same
rule already covered, which means those forbids were asserting something the
analyzer got right for a different reason than the one the code gives:

  the `varname` lookup in the `uses` branch is redundant with
  `isWrittenCalleeName` AND with `namedChildCount !== 1`. Remove any one of the
  three and `\&{ $self->{slot} }` is still refused by the other two. That is
  defence in depth, and it is worth having -- but it is not something a single
  guard's forbid can test.

  `literalNameIn`'s node-type gate and its `$` test are each redundant with
  `isWrittenCalleeName`, which rejects a sigil. Remove either and
  `$self->isa($self->{cls})` and `$self->isa("Other::$suffix")` are still
  refused, because their text starts with `$` and a sigil is not a written name.

So the fixes are in the SOURCE and not in the expectation, because the forbids
were already asserting the right thing and only the analyzer had no shape that
reached them:

  56   \&run               self-reference by CODE REFERENCE, inside `sub run`.
                           REFUSED. Without line 56 the self-reference guard in
                           the `uses` branch is untested -- this forbid could not
                           fire on any line the fixture wrote.
  62   ->render('Not::AClass')   a method call with a LITERAL argument that names
                           nothing any query asks about. `render` is not
                           isa/DOES/can, so no type is being named and there is
                           no `references` edge. This is the control for the
                           query-method gate: remove that gate and this line
                           publishes a class named `Not::AClass`, which is the
                           phantom-type defect class this lane has removed twice.

The mutation set that CANNOT die is not registered, and saying so is part of the
result: a mutant registered against a guard that a second guard already covers
cannot fail, so registering it would be registering a claim the harness does not
support. The redundant guards are declared here with the evidence that they are
redundant, and the load-bearing ones each have a mutant that dies.

expectRelationships.note: a code reference NAMES the sub and invokes nothing. The line is the `varname`'s own line, which is where `helper` is written -- M59's rule that the edge carries the line that names it, not the line of the enclosing statement (line 16 is the comment, 17 is the code).

\&helper() is a reference to a CALL. The call is real and is filed once, under `calls` -- and its target is `helper`, NOT `&helper`. Before the strip this row read `&helper`, a name no symbol carries; the same defect was 93 edges in 36 corpus files.

a class named in a query and not invoked. `Other::Class` leaf-qualifies to `Class`, the same convention `instantiates` already used for `Util.constructor`. The `calls run -> isa` edge beside it is correct and is pinned separately -- `isa` IS a method this line invokes.
the control for the row above. `$self->isa(...)` really does invoke a method named `isa`, so the `calls` edge is right and the two labels are about two different facts about one line.
a role named in a query. `DOES` is perl's role-satisfaction test, so the target is a Trait when the file declares one and a name otherwise -- which is what the leaf convention already gives.

a METHOD named in a query. `later` is declared at line 59 in this same file, so this edge resolves at BOTH ends without leaving the file -- which is the bar `calls` deliberately does not claim and this label can.

forbidRelationships.note: self-reference by method is refused (line 44). A self-edge is true of the source and useless in a graph; the same rule as the self-base guard on `extends`.

THE MEASURED GAP, pinned as absent. `my $t = $TIMEOUT;` on line 53 reads a package global this file declares, and no `uses` edge is emitted for it: the probe measured 2 such reads in 40 files against 850 declaration sites. Declared in the lane doc's limitations with that number, so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
self-reference by package is refused (line 46): `$self->isa('Code::Ref')` inside `package Code::Ref` asks the class whether it is itself.

an INTERPOLATED literal is not a name (line 48). `"Other::$suffix"` is the same node type as `'Other::Class'` and only the `$` distinguishes them, so this forbid is what makes the allowlist positive rather than permissive.
a VARIABLE passed to `isa` states no name (line 38). 175 corpus sites of this shape are refused.

\&{ $self->{slot} } (line 26) is a refgen with a `code_deref_expression` child, not a `varname` -- nothing is written that names a sub. 3,618 corpus sites of non-written code-reference targets are refused on this rule, and a sigil-stripping emitter would have fabricated every one of them.
\@LIST (line 31) is a ref to an ARRAY. The refgen has no `function` child at all, so this cannot be reached even in principle -- pinned so the rule is asserted rather than assumed.

THE REGRESSION PIN for the `&` strip. This row was the analyzer's actual output before the fix, in 93 edges across 36 corpus files, and it could never resolve: the symbol the indexer stores is `helper`. Deleting the strip turns this forbid red.

line 62 is the control for the query-method gate. `render` is not isa/DOES/can, so the literal names nothing that is being QUERIED; without the gate this line publishes a type `Not::AClass`, leaf-qualified to `AClass` like every other target in this lane. That is the phantom-type defect class this lane has removed twice.

line 56 is the self-reference guard for the CODE-REFERENCE branch, the same rule the self-base guard applies to `extends`. This row could not fire before line 56 existed, which is why five mutants survived the first run.

line 68, `&print("hello\n")`. `print` is a PERL BUILTIN and the `&` is sigil, so the builtin probe has to see through it. The pre-review builtin list being 10 words short produced phantom call edges on mojo, and this is the same mechanism one level along: a probe handed `&print` misses the set. FORBIDDEN rather than expected, because the correct answer is that this line emits NOTHING.

line 29, `\&$plain`. If the name guards on the code-reference target are removed TOGETHER, the refgen's first named child is a `scalar` and the target becomes the variable's own text. Kept as a wildcard forbid (no `from`) so it holds whatever sub the edge is attributed to.
